title: A provider limit pauses staffing: the wrapper tees seat output, classifies the exit, refunds the attempt and parks the provider until the reset
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-2723a9b400984ab7b1b10f97c3523c81. dependsOn child 1 (task-756d81f117fb4ef6aeca2c676f433c91: classifySeatExit, createOutputTail, recordSeatExit/recordProviderPause/readProviderPause). Filed by architect-16a01670 2026-09-04, measured at main 68eb1c5d. Verify child 1 first: `ls apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/seat-exit-classifier.ts seat-output-tail.ts provider-pause-ledger.ts`.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the wrapper/spawner behaviour. No read route, no UI, no docs (child 3).

MEASURED (re-measure before planning):
- Spawner: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts (417 lines, pre-existing over-cap - minimal edit, record the size) spawns with `stdio: ["pipe", "inherit", "inherit"]` (:157); the exit is `AgentProcessFailureError(reason, exitCode, signal)` (:196-204) or the resolved `exit` promise; `[wrapper] <item> agent exited <code>` logged at :314; the hard timeout kill at :331.
- Lifetime: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-staffing.ts (145 lines) `trackLifetime(input, exit, retire)` (:76-90) runs `cleanupAuthority(true)` + `retire()` on resolve AND reject - the claim release + session close already happen there through createAgentAuthorityCleanup (agent-authority-cleanup.ts:74).
- Attempts: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:155-159 (`maxItemAttempts`, `attempts` map), :340-346 (leaving READY re-arms), :362-370 (charged at spawn: `attempts.set(workItemId, tried + 1)` unless a GATE_REFUSAL), STAFFING_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED at :364. The wrapper has `config.clock`? (measure: the knobs at wrapper-knobs.ts, `now` sources in agent-wrapper.ts:228-234 use Date.now() - inject a clock port for the pause gate so the tests can move time). The seat command/provider: agent-wrapper-main.ts passes the command; `providerFor(command)` (moe-up-credentials.ts:143) yields the leaf.
- Log lines are the operator's only wrapper UI today (`[wrapper] ...`, `[lander] ...`, `[publisher] ...`).

FEATURE: (1) Spawner: stdout/stderr become "pipe"; each chunk is written verbatim to the wrapper's own process.stdout/process.stderr (byte-identical console output) AND pushed into child 1's `createOutputTail()`; on exit the spawner exposes `{ exitCode, signal, tail: tail.lines() }` to the lifetime (extend the exit promise's resolution/rejection with the tail - the FailureError gains a `tail` field; a resolved exit resolves with the tail). (2) Lifetime: on exit, `classifySeatExit({ provider, exitCode, signal, tail })` from child 1; `recordSeatExit(...)` for EVERY exit (COMPLETED/FAILED/PROVIDER_LIMIT); on PROVIDER_LIMIT: `recordProviderPause({ provider, resetAt: classified.resetAt ?? now + 30 min, since: now, cause })`, REFUND the attempt (`attempts.set(item, max(0, tried - 1))` through a callback the wrapper hands the staffing state), log `[wrapper] provider limit: <provider> paused until <resetAt> (<lastLine>)`; the existing cleanup (claim release + session close) runs unchanged. (3) Wrapper pass: before staffing, `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, now)`; while a pause is live for the seat's provider the pass staffs NOTHING for that provider, reports `surfaceOutcome: "PROVIDER_PAUSED"`-style outcome in the RunOnceReport (name it; the idle log line at agent-wrapper-main.ts:384 prints once per distinct state), and keeps polling; the first pass at or after resetAt staffs normally. A FAILED exit keeps today's attempt behaviour byte-for-byte.
definitionOfDone: Spawner test: with a fake child that writes 'hello' to stdout and the claude limit line to stderr then exits 1, the wrapper process's stdout/stderr receive the SAME bytes (spy on the writable, byte-equal) and the exit carries `tail` containing both lines in order; a child exiting 0 resolves with its tail; the hard-timeout kill path still produces its existing log line (existing spawner tests green unchanged, count line quoted).

Wrapper test (fake spawn + injected clock, real store): a seat exit classified PROVIDER_LIMIT leaves the item's attempt count unchanged (charged at spawn, refunded at exit - assert the count observed on the NEXT pass equals the pre-spawn count), records `moe-seat-exit/1` and `moe-provider-pause/1` (read back from the store), logs `[wrapper] provider limit: claude paused until <resetAt> (...)`, and the claim is released + the session closed by the existing cleanup (store shows WorkReleased + SessionClosed); the next N passes before resetAt spawn nothing for that provider and report the paused outcome; the first pass at resetAt spawns; a FAILED exit consumes the attempt exactly as today (existing attempt-exhaustion arms green unchanged).

A limit line with no reset instant pauses for the bounded default (30 minutes from the exit; constant exported and named in the log line) and staffs again after it; a second PROVIDER_LIMIT within a live pause extends nothing (one pause record per limit exit, read returns the latest).

Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`; agent-spawner.ts grows by no more than 25 lines (pre-existing 417 recorded), agent-wrapper.ts and agent-wrapper-staffing.ts stay under 400 (`wc -l` quoted; extract the pause gate into a sibling module if needed).
taskRails: BYTE-IDENTICAL CONSOLE: teeing the seat's output must not change what the operator sees in the wrapper console; assert byte equality.
NEVER RELEASE OR RETIRE TWICE: the existing exit cleanup stays the single release path; classification only adds records, a refund and a gate.

FAILED stays FAILED: unmatched exits keep today's attempt behaviour byte-for-byte (existing tests unchanged). Refusals/records assert exact values; mutate to prove red (global rail 1). Minimal edits to the over-cap spawner; <=250 lines per new production source.

Add: `export interface SeatExitReport { readonly exitCode: number | null; readonly signal: NodeJS.Signals | null; readonly tail: readonly string[] }` (what one finished seat left behind: exit facts plus the bounded output tail); `export type SeatExitReading = "COMPLETED" | "FAILED" | "PROVIDER_LIMIT"` (how the wrapper read the exit; a limit exit is the PROVIDER's state, never the item's failure); `export interface ProviderPauseFacts { readonly provider: string; readonly resetAt: string; readonly since: string }`. LANDED API from child 1 (task-756d81f117fb4ef6aeca2c676f433c91) - plan against these symbols, they are real on the branch. All under `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/`, all pure, no spawner/wrapper/route/UI change. Import via the `.js` bridges.

FROM `./seat-exit-classifier.js`:
- `classifySeatExit(input: { exitAt: string; exitCode: number | null; provider: string; signal: string | null; tail: readonly string[] }): SeatExitClassification` where `SeatExitClassification = Readonly<{ kind: "COMPLETED"|"FAILED"|"PROVIDER_LIMIT"; lastLine: string | null; matched: string | null; resetAt: string | null }>` (frozen). Rules: `exitCode === 0` -> COMPLETED, whatever the tail says. Otherwise the LAST 40 tail lines are scanned NEWEST-FIRST against the roster entries whose `provider` equals `input.provider`; first match -> PROVIDER_LIMIT with `matched` = the roster id and `resetAt` = the entry's parser or null. No match -> FAILED with `lastLine` = the last non-empty tail line. NOTE FOR YOUR SPAWNER EDIT: `exitAt` is an INPUT, not a clock read - pass the seat's exit instant as ISO. An unknown `provider` string classifies FAILED (empty roster slice), never a limit.
- `SEAT_EXIT_KINDS` = ["COMPLETED","FAILED","PROVIDER_LIMIT"].
- `SEAT_EXIT_ROSTER: readonly SeatExitRosterEntry[]`, frozen, 5 entries `{capturedFrom, id, pattern, provider, resetOf, sample}`. Ids and capture sources: `claude/session-limit` (LIVE seat #4 exit 1, UnAI drive 2026-09-03 21:04 Asia/Jerusalem; composer corroborated in claude.exe 2.1.260 H0()); `claude/usage-limit` (claude.exe 2.1.260 H0 call site); `claude/weekly-limit` (2.1.260 IL.seven_day); `claude/rate-limit` (2.1.260 SDo() case "rate_limit" - carries a DURATION, so `resetOf` is null and `resetAt` comes back null); `codex/usage-limit` (LIVE `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "say hi"` 2026-09-04T17:36:55Z, codex-cli 0.152.0, exit 1, stderr).
- `resolveResetInstant(text: string, exitAt: string): string | null` (re-exported from `./seat-reset-instant.js`). Reads the claude wall clock `[Sep 8, ]10:46am (Asia/Jerusalem)` with the parens OPTIONAL (both real builds), the codex dated `Sep 8th, 2026 10:46 AM` (resolved in UTC - codex prints host-local with no zone, so UTC is the conservative read: it lands the instant LATER for eastern zones), and a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` -> midnight UTC. Returns null on an unknown zone or garbage, and `kind` STAYS PROVIDER_LIMIT in that case - so your gate must treat `resetAt: null` as "limit hit, instant unknown", not as "no limit".

FROM `./seat-output-tail.js`:
- `createOutputTail(options?: { maxBytes?: number; maxLines?: number })` (defaults 16384 / 40) -> `{ bytes(): number; lines(): readonly string[]; push(chunk: Buffer | string): void }`. `push` takes exactly what a stream `data` event hands over; one `TextDecoder(..., {stream: true})` lives for the tail's life so a multi-byte sequence split across chunks is not corrupted. `lines()` returns a FROZEN copy INCLUDING a partial trailing line, so a seat killed mid-line still yields its last words. Bounds apply per line inside `push`, line cap first then byte cap; a lone over-long line is TRUNCATED to its last maxBytes rather than dropped. This is the module the row description said must exist so your spawner edit stays minimal - agent-spawner.ts was already 417 lines.
- YOUR TEE: the spawner currently starts the seat `stdio: ["pipe","inherit","inherit"]` (agent-spawner.ts:157). Switching stdout/stderr to "pipe" means the wrapper must write them onward BYTE-FOR-BYTE itself; feed the same chunks to `push`.

FROM `./provider-pause-ledger.js` (re-exports everything from `./provider-pause-contracts.js`, so one import gets it all):
- `recordSeatExit(store, { decidedAt, exitCode, kind, lastLine, projectId, provider, resetAt, sessionId, workItemId })` -> `{ok:true, record, replayed} | {ok:false, code:"SEAT_EXIT_RECORD_INVALID"|"EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT"}`.
- `recordProviderPause(store, { cause: {lastLine, workItemId} | null, projectId, provider, resetAt, since })` -> same result shape with `code:"PROVIDER_PAUSE_RECORD_INVALID"|"EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT"`.
- `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, now): ProviderPauseRecordV1 | null` - the LATEST record, answered only while `resetAt > now` STRICTLY (at the reset instant the limit is over). An unparseable `now` returns null by design (an unreadable clock must not park a fleet).
- `clearProviderPause(store, { now, projectId, provider })` - a pause record with `resetAt = now`; one event type, one read rule.
- Constants: `SEAT_EXIT_COMMAND_KIND` "internal.wrapper.seat_exit", `PROVIDER_PAUSE_COMMAND_KIND` "internal.wrapper.provider_pause", `AGENT_WRAPPER_PRINCIPAL_ID` "daemon:agent-wrapper", `SEAT_EXIT_VERSION` "moe-seat-exit/1", `PROVIDER_PAUSE_VERSION` "moe-provider-pause/1", `LAST_LINE_MAX_CHARS` 512. Aggregates: `providerPauseAggregateId(projectId, provider)` = `provider-pause:<projectId>:<provider>`, `seatExitAggregateId(projectId, sessionId)` = `seat-exit:<projectId>:<sessionId>`.
- Both kinds ride `store.commitExpectedVersionDecision` and are ABSENT from the daemon command registry, the vocabulary and the MCP allowlist (verified: `internal.wrapper` occurs repo-wide only at provider-pause-contracts.ts:21-22). Do NOT register them - that is deliberate, they are wrapper-side facts nobody may forge from the browser.
- Command ids are DERIVED from the inputs (`seatExitRecordId(projectId, sessionId, decidedAt)`, `providerPauseRecordId(projectId, provider, since)`), so a wrapper retry REPLAYS instead of double-writing; check `replayed` if you care which happened.

TWO THINGS TO PLAN AROUND, both recorded on child 1 with detail: (a) `readProviderPause` currently folds the whole decision ledger (no aggregate-scoped decision read exists on the store) - if your gate calls it on a hot path, raise it; (b) a clear whose `now` equals the pause's `since` to the millisecond replays the pause instead of clearing it (fail-safe: the pause persists).
